title: observability-weekly-2026-03-02
content:
OBSERVABILITY TEAM - WEEKLY NOTES (2026-03-02)

Attendees: Aisha P., Marco L., Sasha R., Priya D., Ethan B. (notes are rough - working doc)

Objective: sync on tracing rollout, dashboard refresh improvements, and cost telemetry discrepancies for Dedicated customers. Capture standup updates, blockers, decisions, and action items.

---
SUMMARY HIGHLIGHTS
- Tracing: sampling pipeline POC passed end-to-end in staging; prod rollout gated on span size reduction (INF-1450).
- Dashboards: slow refresh on per-route cost dashboards due to large BigQuery joins; short-term caching reduces load but needs infra review.
- Cost telemetry: misattribution of Dedicated vs Hosted requests in the billing feed found; root cause is routing metadata drop for fallback routing. Hotfix planned.

---
STANDUP LOG (individual updates, 15m standup style)
- Aisha: reviewing INF-1450 PR, confirmed sampling config works in staging with 1% sampling on high-card spans. Need decisions on default sample rates + rollout plan. Working with SRE bench to validate p95 CPU under load.
- Marco: dashboards — implemented in-memory caching layer for per-route cost dashboard; refresh times down from ~90s -> ~12s in staging. Observed stale counter windows; will add TTL and invalidation on model deploy.
- Sasha: tracing exporter — noticed span payload sizes up 25% after last serializer change. Working on compacting attributes and dropping redundant tags. Will run impact test with QA trace load.
- Priya: cost telemetry — identified fallback routing path strips routing metadata (missing x-redwood-route header on internal retries). Drafting hotfix to restore metadata on retries; will also add an assertion in integration test.
- Ethan: alerts/runbooks — updating runbooks for slow dashboard refresh and tracing backlog. Added playbook steps for diagnosing exporter backpressure.

---
METRICS / OBSERVATIONS (most recent)
- p95 trace ingestion latency (prod): 220ms (target < 200ms)
- trace export CPU on trace-relay nodes: 68% avg (spike to 95% during deploys)
- dashboard per-route query time: median 12s (after caching), 95th 28s
- cost telemetry misattribution rate: 6% of Dedicated requests incorrectly labelled (goal 0.5%)
- sampling POC (staging): reduced ingested spans by ~72% with 1% sample for hot routes

---
DECISIONS MADE
- Proceed with staged rollout of sampling + span compaction. Stage 1: low-risk routes (non-billing) 2026-03-05; Stage 2: high-volume routes 2026-03-12 — contingent on trace export CPU staying < 80%.
- Hotfix for routing metadata restore prioritized and scheduled for 2026-03-03 morning (INF-1450-hotfix).
- Short-term dashboard caching is acceptable as a stopgap; infra ticket to evaluate BigQuery cost/perf alternatives (see linked INF ticket).

---
BLOCKERS / RISKS
- Risk: sampling reduces visibility for rare failure modes. Mitigation: keep full tracing for error-only samples and maintain a high-fidelity sample path for 0.1% of traffic.
- Blocker: need SRE approval on increased egress quotas before pushing export throughput changes. Raised SRE ticket SRE-778.
- Risk: dedicated customer billing correctness SLA breach if hotfix delayed. Pager on-call if hotfix misses 2026-03-03 window.

---
ACTION ITEMS (owner — due)
- Marco Li — finalize TTL/invalidation for dashboard cache and instrument cache hit metrics — due 2026-03-04
- Sasha Romanov — implement span attribute compaction and run stage load test (PR opened) — due 2026-03-06
- Priya Desai — deploy routing metadata hotfix to prod and monitor misattribution metric — due 2026-03-03 morning
- Aisha Patel — coordinate staged sampling rollout plan and update confluence doc with runbook + rollback steps — due 2026-03-04
- Ethan Brown — complete runbook edits and add alert thresholds for trace export CPU > 85% and dashboard query p95 > 25s — due 2026-03-04
- Team — schedule post-rollout verification session 48h after each stage (calendar invite) — owner: Aisha — due 2026-03-05

---
MEETING NOTES / DISCUSSION POINTS (raw)
- Discussion: default sampling rate debate. Marco worried about missing DEBUG-level traces for low-frequency errors; Sasha suggested dynamic sampling tied to error rate per route. Action: prototype dynamic sampler in staging.
- Priya pointed out an edge case where internal retries from dedicated pools go through fallback and lose x-redwood-route header — this is the current misattribution vector. Proposed adding integration test to fail on header loss.
- Consideration: BigQuery cost increases if we continue to naively join large billing tables for per-customer dashboards. Options: pre-aggregates, materialized views, or move heavy joins to nightly ETL. Infra to evaluate.
- Note: function-calling traces include large JSON payloads; decide to redact payload fields beyond 2KB before span export. Sasha to propose regex-based redaction rules.

---
PARKING LOT / FUTURE WORK
- Evaluate moving heavy dashboard queries to a dedicated OLAP cluster (cost analysis required).
- Long-term: replace current trace store with sharded, compressed backend if sampling insufficient. Cost/benefit doc required.
- Add more golden traces and automated regression checks to catch sampling-induced signal loss.

---
QUICK LINKS / RESOURCES
- Tracing sampling proposal (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/123456/Tracing+Sampling+Proposal
- INF ticket tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1450
- PR for span compaction: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/456
- Slack discussion: slack thread (observability): slack://channel?team=T12345&id=COBS1234&thread_ts=1700000000

---
NOTES TO SELF (loose/thoughts)
- double-check cost impact of pre-aggregates vs streaming transforms.
- remember to include Dedicated customers in post-hotfix verification and ask CS to validate billing sample.
- TODO: add a short checklist for rolling back sampling if error signal drops > 20% for critical routes.

End of notes.
